section: Scheduled Tribes - Forest Rights Act 2006, Fifth and Sixth Schedules, TSP, Eklavya schools
subsections: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate

accepted.s: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission, constituted in 1953, is associated with which of the following observations regarding Scheduled Tribes?
o: Tribal communities are identified exclusively on the basis of geographical isolation
Tribal communities are defined only by their economic backwardness
Tribes must profess a particular religion
Tribes generally lead a separate and exclusive existence and may belong to any religion
accepted.x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission stated that Scheduled Tribes lived a separate and exclusive existence, while also recognising that tribes could belong to any religion.
accepted.tq: Use the mandate rather than confusing the commission with later committees on land alienation or ST criteria.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
a. Verrier Elwin Committee
b. U.N. Dhebar Commission
c. Lokur Committee
d. Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee

List-II (Associated subject or outcome)
i. Criteria for defining Scheduled Tribes
ii. Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks
iii. PESA Act, 1996
iv. Tribal condition and land alienation

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: Verrier Elwin dealt with Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks; Dhebar examined tribal conditions and land alienation; Lokur dealt with ST criteria; and Dilip Singh Bhuria was associated with PESA 1996.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong committee-mandate association.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Kaka Kalelkar — 1953
2. Verrier Elwin — 1959
3. U.N. Dhebar — 1960–61
4. Lokur — 1973

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kaka Kalelkar, Verrier Elwin and U.N. Dhebar are correctly matched with 1953, 1959 and 1960–61 respectively. The Lokur Committee was constituted in 1965, not 1973.
accepted.tq: Check the dates individually and identify the swapped-year trap in the last pair.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The category of Primitive Tribal Groups, later termed Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, followed the work of which commission in 1973?
accepted.x: The Primitive Tribal Group category followed the work of the U.N. Dhebar Commission, which examined tribal conditions and land alienation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between committees by linking the later category to the commission’s mandate.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who chaired the committee that examined the criteria for defining Scheduled Tribes in 1965?
accepted.x: The 1965 Lokur Committee, headed by B.N. Lokur, examined the criteria for defining Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Test the chair separately from the committee’s subject to avoid confusing neighbouring tribal committees.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding committees associated with tribal communities:

1. The Kalelkar Commission was constituted under Article 340.
2. The Bhuria Committee of 1991 was associated with the PESA Act, 1996.
3. The Bhuria Commission of 2002–04 dealt with tribal advancement, including land reform and the concerns of tribal women and children.
4. The Xaxa Committee was set up by the Planning Commission in 2013.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Xaxa Committee was set up by the PMO, not the Planning Commission.
accepted.tq: The wrong-authority trap is used in statement 4 by replacing the PMO with a neighbouring central institution.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 2013 high-level committee chaired by Professor Virginius Xaxa primarily examined which of the following?
o: The socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities
The working of Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks
accepted.x: The Xaxa Committee, set up by the PMO in 2013, examined the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities and reported in 2014.
accepted.tq: Match the recent committee with its broad mandate rather than with an older constitutional subject.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their constitution:

A. Lokur Committee
B. Kaka Kalelkar Commission
C. Xaxa Committee
D. U.N. Dhebar Commission
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953), U.N. Dhebar Commission (1960–61), Lokur Committee (1965) and Xaxa Committee (2013).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two middle committees by year.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two bodies associated with Dilip Singh Bhuria?
o: The 1991 Bhuria Committee examined tribal health, while the 2002–04 Commission examined Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks
The 1991 Bhuria Committee was linked to PESA, while the 2002–04 Bhuria Commission addressed tribal advancement and related reforms
The 1991 Bhuria Committee dealt with forest rights, while the 2002–04 Commission dealt with ST identification
Both bodies were constituted in 2002–04 for the same mandate
accepted.x: The Bhuria Committee of 1991 led to PESA 1996, whereas the Bhuria Commission of 2002–04 focused on tribal advancement, funds, land reform, and tribal women and children.
accepted.tq: Separate similar names by comparing their years and distinct mandates.
accepted.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The nodal Ministry for implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 is the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
accepted.tq: Use the who-is-responsible test to distinguish the nodal ministry from ministries involved in implementation.

accepted.s: Under Section 6 of the Forest Rights Act, 2006, which body initiates the process of determining the nature and extent of individual and community forest rights?
accepted.x: The Gram Sabha initiates the determination process and passes resolutions on claims under Section 6 of the Forest Rights Act.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority test: distinguish the initiating grassroots body from committees that subsequently examine claims.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the processing of claims under the Forest Rights Act, 2006:

1. The Gram Sabha passes resolutions on claims.
2. Claims are examined by Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees.
3. Each of these committees consists of six members.
4. The committees include representatives of revenue, tribal and forest authorities and elected panchayat members.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Gram Sabha initiates and resolves claims, while six-member Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees examine claims and issue titles.
accepted.tq: Check the complete institutional sequence from Gram Sabha initiation to committee examination and title issuance.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT recognised as a forest right under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: Automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land
Habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
accepted.x: The Act recognises rights such as minor forest produce, community forest resource management and PVTG habitat rights. It does not confer automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the statutory list of individual and community forest rights.

accepted.s: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 was enacted primarily to address what was described as the historical injustice to:
accepted.x: The Act’s full title concerns recognition of forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, and its stated objective was to undo historical injustice to forest dwellers.
accepted.tq: Use the stated legislative purpose rather than confusing beneficiaries with implementing agencies.

accepted.s: A forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribe family claims recognition of rights under the Forest Rights Act. Which date is relevant for determining occupation of forest land?
accepted.x: Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes must have been occupying the forest land before 13 December 2005 for eligibility under the stated cut-off criterion.
accepted.tq: Treat the cut-off date as a direct numerical-recall point and reject nearby constitutional or enactment dates.

accepted.s: For recognition under the Forest Rights Act, Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must establish residence in or dependence on forests for:
accepted.x: Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence in or dependence on forests for three generations, specified as 75 years, before 2005.
accepted.tq: Separate the generation requirement from the ST cut-off date and convert it into the stated year equivalent.

accepted.s: What is the maximum extent of forest rights that may be recognised per family under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
accepted.x: The ceiling for forest rights is up to four hectares per family.
accepted.tq: Test the statutory ceiling directly using close numerical distractors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an individual forest right rather than a community forest right?
accepted.x: Habitation and self-cultivation are individual rights. Nistar, grazing, fishing and community forest resource management are examples of community rights.
accepted.tq: Separate individual and community rights by identifying the beneficiary and nature of use.

accepted.s: A Gram Sabha recommends diversion of a limited portion of forest land for a school or dispensary. Which statement is correct?
o: Such diversion is completely prohibited under the Act
It is allowed without any recommendation or area limit
It can be approved only by a private timber company
It may be allowed for public utilities on Gram Sabha recommendation, subject to the stated limit of up to one hectare per project
accepted.x: Forest land may be diverted for public utilities such as schools and dispensaries on Gram Sabha recommendation, with the stated limit of up to one hectare per project.
accepted.tq: Apply the exception for public utilities while checking both the recommending authority and the area limit.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship between the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and inconsistent laws?
o: The Act is subordinate to every earlier forest law
The Act applies only where no State law exists
The Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with it
The Act can be overridden by an executive circular alone
accepted.x: The Forest Rights Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with its provisions.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed legal relationship between the Act and inconsistent laws.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in the order in which the first PVTG habitat rights were recognised as stated below:

A. Baiga
B. Bharia
C. Kamar
accepted.x: Bharia in Madhya Pradesh was the first PVTG mentioned, followed by Kamar and Baiga in Chhattisgarh.
accepted.tq: Identify the first item and then preserve the stated sequence of the subsequent communities.

accepted.s: The first Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group stated to have received habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act framework was:
accepted.x: Bharia of Madhya Pradesh was the first PVTG mentioned as receiving habitat rights; Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh followed.
accepted.tq: Use the first-in-sequence trap to distinguish Bharia from the later Kamar and Baiga claims.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about habitat rights for PVTGs is correct?
o: They follow the 2014 Ministry of Tribal Affairs guidelines, with coordination by four State departments and assistance from UNDP
They are governed exclusively by the Ministry of Environment without State-level coordination
They were introduced through the 1953 Kalelkar Commission alone
They can be granted only to non-tribal forest dwellers
accepted.x: The habitat-rights framework follows 2014 Ministry of Tribal Affairs guidelines. Forest, Revenue, Tribal and Panchayati Raj departments coordinate, with UNDP assistance.
accepted.tq: Check both the guideline year and the complete set of coordinating departments before selecting the precise statement.

accepted.s: Which one of the following claims regarding PVTG habitat rights is INCORRECT?
o: Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh followed Bharia
Habitat rights are among the rights recognised for PVTGs
Bharia of Madhya Pradesh was the first group mentioned
Baiga were the first PVTG to receive habitat rights
accepted.x: Baiga were not the first in the stated sequence. Bharia of Madhya Pradesh was first, followed by Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh.
accepted.tq: Use the first-versus-later distinction to detect the reversed sequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Lokur criteria for identifying Scheduled Tribes?
o: Mandatory adherence to a specified religion
accepted.x: The Lokur criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness. Mandatory adherence to a specified religion is not a criterion.
accepted.tq: Use the religion-neutral principle to reject an absolute condition absent from the criteria.
accepted.sec: ST identification - criteria, procedure, religion  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following as criteria associated with the Lokur Committee:

1. Primitive traits
2. Distinctive culture
3. Geographical isolation
4. Shyness of contact
5. Backwardness

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All five listed features are the criteria associated with the Lokur Committee for defining Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Treat a complete enumerated list as an all-correct option only after checking every item.
accepted.sec: ST identification - criteria, procedure, religion  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the procedure for inclusion of a community as a Scheduled Tribe?
o: State proposal → Registrar General of India → NCST → Union Cabinet → Parliament amends the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950
NCST proposal → State Cabinet → President directly amends the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950
State proposal → Parliament → Registrar General of India → Supreme Court
Registrar General of India → State proposal → Union Cabinet → NCST
accepted.x: The stated sequence is proposal by the State, examination by the Registrar General of India and NCST, consideration by the Union Cabinet, and amendment by Parliament under Article 342(2).
accepted.tq: Follow the institutional sequence from initiation to the final constitutional amendment authority.
accepted.sec: ST identification - criteria, procedure, religion  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under which provision is Parliament empowered to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 for the purpose of modifying the list of Scheduled Tribes?
accepted.x: Article 342(2) provides for Parliament to include or exclude groups from the list of Scheduled Tribes by law.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the procedural provision for amendment from the definitional provision in Article 366(25).
accepted.sec: ST identification - criteria, procedure, religion  [other exams]

accepted.s: The constitutional definition of the expression “Scheduled Tribes” is provided in:
accepted.x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes by reference to the tribes or tribal communities deemed to be Scheduled Tribes under Article 342.
accepted.tq: Separate the definitional article from the article dealing with notification and amendment of the ST list.
accepted.sec: ST identification - criteria, procedure, religion  [other exams]
